Topic B — Thermal Runaway in a Packed-Bed Reactor

Darcy flow · coupled species and energy with Arrhenius kinetics · Robin wall cooling · tier: standard

Motivation

An exothermic reaction in a cooled packed bed heats itself; the heat release grows exponentially with temperature (Arrhenius), the wall removes heat only linearly. Above a critical inlet temperature the hot spot grows steeply — the classical thermal-runaway / ignition problem (Semenov, van Heerden, Bilous–Amundson). You will compute the hot-spot temperature and the conversion as functions of the inlet temperature.

Course weeks: 8–9 (residual, Newton, continuation), 12 (Darcy), 13 (advection–diffusion, SUPG). New: two fields coupled through one exponential source.

Model

Bed \Omega=[0,4]\times[0,1], flow in +x. Lumped, dimensionless units (\rho C_p=1).

Flow — Darcy, homogeneous: \mathbf u=-\frac{\kappa}{\mu}\nabla p, \nabla\cdot\mathbf u=0; pressure drop between inlet and outlet, no flux through the walls (mixed form RT×DG as in Week 12, or the pressure Poisson equation and \mathbf u=-\kappa\nabla p/\mu — justify your choice).

Species and energy, solved together (one mixed space, one NonlinearProblem): \mathbf u\cdot\nabla c-\nabla\cdot(D\nabla c)=-R(c,T),\qquad \mathbf u\cdot\nabla T-\nabla\cdot(k\nabla T)=\Delta H\,R(c,T),\qquad R=k_0\,e^{-E/T}\,c, with c=1, T=T_\text{in} at x=0; natural outflow at x=4; on the walls y=0,1: \partial_nc=0 and Newton cooling -k\,\partial_nT=h_w\,(T-T_\text{amb}), T_\text{amb}=T_\text{in}.

Design output: peak temperature T_{\max} and outlet conversion X=1-\int_\text{out}u\,c\,ds/\int_\text{in}u\,c\,ds against T_\text{in}.

Note

Analysis questions (required). (i) Linearise the residual at (c,T): which term can destroy coercivity of the Jacobian, and how does its size depend on E/T^2? (ii) Adiabatic bound: for equal diffusivities (D=k, Lewis number 1) show that \theta=T+\Delta H\,c satisfies a linear advection–diffusion equation and, with the cooled walls, the maximum principle gives T\le T_\text{in}+\Delta H. What can happen when D\ne k? (iii) The cell Péclet number of the suggested parameters — do you need SUPG?

Suggested parameters

\kappa/\mu=1 with a pressure drop giving |\mathbf u|\approx1; D=0.01, k=0.05 (or D=k for the bound check); \Delta H=2; E=10; h_w and k_0 chosen so that cooling competes with heat release (e.g. start with k_0=5, h_w=5); T_\text{in}\in[1,2.5]. Finding parameters that give a steep but single-valued curve is part of the task: very steep curves signal multiple steady states (topic E).

Required tasks

  1. Darcy flow, species with a fixed temperature, energy with a prescribed heat source — each verified on its own.
  2. The coupled (c,T) problem with Newton and continuation in T_\text{in} (previous solution as the initial guess, Week 9/15).
  3. The curves T_{\max}(T_\text{in}) and X(T_\text{in}), with Newton iteration counts and SNES reasons along the sweep.
  4. Mesh independence at the steepest part of the curve (two or more meshes).

Verification specific to this topic

  • Adiabatic bound T_{\max}\le T_\text{in}+\Delta H, checked at every point of the sweep (with D=k it is a theorem; report what you see for D\ne k).
  • Isothermal limit: E=0 gives a linear first-order reaction; for plug flow and negligible axial diffusion X=1-e^{-k_0L/u} (PFR).
  • MMS for the coupled system with the Arrhenius term (source terms from UFL), predicted rates for your elements.

Stretch goals

  1. Cooling design: sweep h_w at fixed T_\text{in}; the smallest h_w that avoids runaway.
  2. Hysteresis: approach the same T_\text{in} from a cold and from a hot initial guess.
  3. A high-permeability channel through the bed: hotter or cooler?
  4. Inverse problem (bonus, §5 of the project guide): estimate E or k_0 from synthetic thermocouple data.

Milestones

M1 Darcy · M2 isothermal species (PFR check) · M3 energy with prescribed source and Robin walls · M4 coupled Newton · M5 sweep and mesh study.

Pitfalls

  • A temperature above the adiabatic bound (for D=k) is a bug — usually a sign error in a source term or an unconverged Newton step.
  • Newton from T=T_\text{in} everywhere at a high k_0 may diverge: continuation in k_0 first, then in T_\text{in}.
  • Bounds: vinewtonrsls with c\ge0 helps when Newton overshoots.

References

  • O. Levenspiel, Chemical Reaction Engineering, 3rd ed., Wiley 1999 — PFR conversion.
  • G. F. Froment, K. B. Bischoff, J. De Wilde, Chemical Reactor Analysis and Design, 3rd ed., Wiley 2011 — packed-bed hot spots, runaway criteria.
